$comment: Managed by copilot-governance. Do not edit this file downstream.
Surface: Claude Code.
THIS IS A FRAGMENT, NOT A FILE TO COPY. Its destination is
.claude/settings.json, which is a real settings file that developers and
other tooling also write to (model, permissions, env, statusline). The sync
must MERGE the 'hooks.UserPromptSubmit' key into any existing file. Copying
this over an existing .claude/settings.json would silently discard the
developer's own settings — the '.fragment' in the filename is there so a
future change to the sync script cannot mistake it for a whole-file asset.
UserPromptSubmit in Claude Code takes NO matcher — the event always fires,
and a matcher field would be silently ignored. So the registration is a flat
array of hook commands, not the matcher-grouped shape used by tool events.
What this surface can actually do (verified 2026-08-02):
Claude Code cannot replace prompt text on any event. The documentation is
explicit that UserPromptSubmit 'can't replace the prompt; it only injects
additionalContext alongside it', and UserPromptExpansion cannot rewrite
either. So the hybrid strategy's rewrite arm is delivered here as injected
context beside the developer's untouched prompt, which preserves the
original wording by construction.
Blocking uses the top-level {"decision":"block","reason":...} form.
permissionDecision is PreToolUse-only and is ignored here.
${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is used rather than a relative path because Claude
Code does not guarantee the hook's working directory is the project root.
Note that VS Code Copilot ALSO reads .claude/settings.json. In a repository
that registers both this fragment and .github/hooks/prompt-interceptor.json,
a VS Code developer will have the governance block injected twice — once
shaped for each surface. That is a token cost, not a correctness failure
(the second copy is identical context, and a Claude-shaped block decision is
simply ignored by VS Code). Where a repository's developers use only one of
the two clients, register only that client's config.
The 'timeout' is in seconds. Claude Code lowers the default command timeout
to 30s for UserPromptSubmit specifically; 10 keeps a slow hook well inside
it, and a timeout fails open.
